specimens.label: Vienna, ÖNB, Cod. 10689/29 — 'Iudicium astrologicum huius geniturae', autograph nativity-judgment draft
specimens.date_basis: ÖNB catalogue (undated 16th c.); subject geniture unnamed
specimens.basis: One of the Vienna Tychonis-Brahe Nachlass papers (Cod. 10689; Dreyer TBOO X notes these bundles 'contain autograph material' used to edit Tycho's Works & Letters). A full-res hand-triage (IIIF surrogate, 17 canvases @ ~5857x8685px): the judgment is a WORKING DRAFT in Tycho's rapid humanist-italic autograph hand — heading 'Iudicium Astrologicum huius geniturae', then a nativity chart/positions table and the judgment under rubric sections 'De Complexione', 'De Amicis et Inimicis', 'De Itinere'. Diagnostic features all match the secure pillars: single-storey cursive a, uncial looped d, long-s + round final-s, looped -que abbreviation, dense macron suspensions, steep rightward slant, rapid ductus — plus AUTHOR-STYLE strike-throughs and interlinear corrections (img 0006, 0009), i.e. composition not transcription. Same genre and hand as the autograph Latin judgment in GKS 1823. Sampled canvases 0006 + 0009 show a single consistent autograph hand; a full leaf-by-leaf confirmation of all 4 leaves is pending. A register-symmetric, feature-by-feature comparison of the judgment prose ('De Amicis et Inimicis') against the SECURE pillar GKS 316 autograph prose ('De occasione interruptarum observationum & discessus mej') supports the same hand: 22 concordances — 19 of them confirmed on a second audit pass — against 4 discordances, all four on LABILE traits (baseline-drift direction, line-spacing, pen-pressure, minim regularity), plausibly genre- or speed-driven, with NO discordance on letterform construction. Two highly distinctive concordances carry the case: the non-closing, leftward-curling g descender, and the curved, hook-shaped (rather than barred) abbreviation marks. The secure/A grade rests on CONVERGENCE — (i) provenance: this is literally a leaf of Tycho's own Nachlass (Cod. 10689), bought with his effects and mined by Dreyer to edit Tycho's Works; (ii) full-diagnostic paleographic match to the pillars; (iii) the draft-with-corrections character (a composer's, not a copyist's, hand); and (iv) the register-symmetric comparison against a secure pillar — a corroboration GKS 316 itself never received. CAVEATS (ENFSI BPM-FHX-01): a comparison at these sample lengths is SUPPORTING evidence, not a forensic identification; the run is modest (~85 words combined) with no overlapping capitals; and unlike GKS 306 there is no independent NAMED-AUTHOR anchor (the geniture is unnamed) — the case is provenance + paleography + comparison, not authorship documentation.
specimens.established_by: full-res hand-triage + register-symmetric comparison; comparison vs secure pillar kb-gks-316 + kb-gks-1823 (autograph judgment); Dreyer TBOO X Prolegomena (Vienna Nachlass)

specimens.label: Copenhagen, KB, GKS 1823 kvart — Horoscope of Duke Hans (1583), partly autograph
specimens.date_basis: KB/thesaurus dating
specimens.basis: KB (Nielsen): partly Tycho's hand; green velvet binding. A facsimile autopsy, sweeping all 131 leaves of the digitised manuscript, found the volume to be bilingual and to divide cleanly by script. The Latin portions — the nativity chart ('Anno 1583 Julii 26. 9.20 Harsleffÿ', with the Tycho-style y-diaeresis), the DIRECTIONES tables (directae and conversae), and the extended first-person Latin judgment prose that opens 'Circa Annum 40 completum / Ascendens sua directione...' and runs on 'Constitui itaque loca Solis et Lunae... emendavi ex observationibus circa eos... saepe praeter omnem spem evasurus' — are in Tycho's humanist-italic autograph, and are consistent with his secure autograph prose across the diagnostic set: rapid humanist italic; single-storey a; long-s with round final-s; uncial looped d; macron suspensions; and a clean rightward slant of |median| ~15 deg (range 14-20 deg), within the same steep band as GKS 316 (~23 deg) and the 1599 leaf (~16-28 deg). This matches KB's 'partly autograph' and the variant's treatment of the horoscope prose as autograph. The second, uniform section is a parallel German translation of the judgment in a German Kurrent chancery cursive, with red section headers ('Vonn Besorgnus') and the quire signature 'a 5' — a DIFFERENT script, NOT Tycho's humanist hand. Its authorship is explained but not resolved: the German Kurrent could be Tycho's own German-script hand (he was bilingual, and the text is first-person — 'mein eigen observation'), or a Danish/German court secretary's translation. Deciding it would need a secure Tycho German-Kurrent comparator — an autograph German letter — and none is held: a sweep of the letter catalogues returns three German letters, all surviving only as printed copies. The German section is therefore left ATTRIBUTION-OPEN, not asserted autograph, leaning to a translator's hand on parsimony alone. Re-examined at higher resolution (268 pages): the script-based delineation holds, and the boundary is located — the nativity chart, the DIRECTIONES tables and the Latin judgment prose are Tycho's autograph, the German translation runs from roughly the hundredth leaf to the end, and the Latin-to-German boundary falls between the ninetieth leaf (still Latin) and the hundred-and-tenth (already German).
specimens.established_by: a facsimile autopsy; hi-res surrogate reconfirmation; Nielsen (S_NIELSEN_BT); KB

OPEN, now likely UNRESOLVABLE by comparison (a browser-based catalogue session/EMLO check): is the German KURRENT section Tycho's own German-script hand or a court secretary's translation? An EMLO sweep (sender=Brahe,Tycho AND language=German) returns exactly 3 German letters (to the Hesse-Kassel court, 1591-92), and ALL survive ONLY as printed copies in Dreyer Opera Omnia vol.6 — there is NO surviving autograph German Tycho letter anywhere in EMLO to use as a comparator. Since no secure Tycho German-Kurrent specimen is known to survive, the German section leans toward a court secretary's translation on parsimony (an autograph would be a unique survival), but this is inference, not proof. If a Tycho German autograph ever surfaces it would both settle this AND open a new German-script register/variant.

specimens.basis: Tycho observation protocol (Wandsbek 1596-97, paper, 208 ff.) whose tabulated distance/time observations are engrossed in a neat upright familia clerk-hand, but which contains at least one SUSTAINED autograph PROSE leaf: f.131v (facsimile TYCH0009), the 'DE OCCASIONE INTERRUPTArum Observationum & discessus mei' first-person narrative of the April 1597 departure from Hven (Insula Venusia), the transfer of instruments, library and printing press to Copenhagen (Haffniam in aedes meas), and the four great instruments left at Stjerneborg. A facsimile autopsy found that this leaf is whole-leaf autograph in Tycho's rapid humanist-italic prose hand — first-person content (discessus mei, aedes meas, reliqui, effigiem meam) plus paleographic consistency with the secure pillars (rapid humanist italic; heavy macron suspensions; dual long-s/round-s distribution; uncial looped d; broad-edge-quill thick/thin shading; ~22 deg rightward slant matching the 8 May 1599 leaf; the word 'discessus' echoing 'discessi' on the 14 Jun 1599 farewell leaf). A NUMERIC comparison vs the album pillars is register-asymmetric (rapid prose vs formal display) so is not the basis; the attribution rests on first-person content + cross-register paleographic consistency. The familia-engrossed observation TABLES (TYCH0000-0008, 0010-0020) are a separate clerk-hand and are NOT autograph.

surrogates.label: 'Tycho Brahe: Observationes planetarum' — digital facsimile edition of GKS 316 fol. ff.127r-137r (Svindborg)

specimens.content: Observation protocol covering 1 Jan 1596 - 20 Oct 1597 (Wandsbek, after the flight from Hven), with Kepler's declaration to Tycho's heirs glued inside the front cover. One of only two Brahe manuscripts in Tycho's hand currently DIGITISED at KB (with GKS 1823). f.131v (TYCH0009) opens: 'DE OCCASIONE INTERRUPTArum Observationum & discessus mei. Postea nullas in Insula Venusia praesens continuavi Observationes; sed statim à Paschatis festo die 29 Aprilis inde cum familiâ discedens, Haffniam in aedes meas Instrumenta Astronomica (paucis exceptis) unà cum totâ supellectile librariâ & Typographiâ successivè transferri curavi. Quae autem istic reliqui, erant hae quatuor: Armilla maxima cum suo aequatore fixo Orichalco inducto & Quadrans Chalybeus magnus...' — i.e. the four great instruments left behind in the Stjerneborg observatory (Observatorio Stellaeburgico) at Hven, with the mural quadrant bearing Tycho's own portrait (effigiem meam). This is the famous first-person 'migratione mea ex patria' autograph narrative — now autograph (a facsimile autopsy) and the observation-log register's first image-backed atlas specimen.
specimens.extent: digitised selection ff.127r-137r (21 leaves, TYCH0000-0020) of a 208-leaf protocol. TWO hands: (1) familia clerk engrossing the tabulated stellar-distance observations (Anno 97, Feb-Oct), (2) Tycho's own rapid autograph prose — the f.131v DE OCCASIONE INTERRUPTARUM narrative (TYCH0009) and the LONGITUDINES ET LATITUDINES rubric (TYCH0008) — plus marginal interventions. The autograph is the prose + interventions, not the tables.

CLERK ATTRIBUTION (, narrowed): the observation TABLES (TYCH0000-0007 etc.) are a single neat humanist-italic engrossing clerk-hand. Dreyer (Tycho Brahe: a picture..., scribe notes) attributes the engrossing of the original-observation volumes to Tycho's WORKSHOP scribes — named Hans Crol and Johannes Aurifaber — plus the calculating assistants. For THIS protocol (1 Jan 1596 - 20 Oct 1597, Hven->Wandsbek) the dead/departed are EXCLUDED: Crol (d.1591), Morsing (d.1590), Flemløse (left Hven c.1589), Gellius Sascerides (departed 1596). The live late-Hven/Wandsbek familia engrossers were LONGOMONTANUS (chief assistant, to 1597) and Johannes Eriksen — Longomontanus the leading candidate. NOT YET by handwriting: positive ID is testable against the secure Longomontanus autograph at ÖNB Cod. lat. 10703 f.236v (letter to Kepler, per Gingerich, Copernicus Census p.186). a browser-based catalogue session Cod. 10703 ('Collectio epistolarum originalium... ad Iohannem Kepler', 398 ff.) is NOT digitised — so this is a Vienna reading-room request, not an online pull (see longomontanus discriminator).

specimens.label: Copenhagen, KB, GKS 306 folio — 1000-star catalogue presentation copy to Christian IV (Wandsbek 1598); autograph preface to Rudolf II
specimens.date_basis: title-leaf colophon 'Wandesburgi Anno [1598]'; KB catalogue; dedication to Christian IV (king from 1596)
specimens.basis: Deluxe parchment presentation copy of the 1000-star catalogue 'Stellarum octavi orbis inerrantium accurata restitutio' (Wandsbek 1598), dedicated to King Christian IV of Denmark. A hi-res surrogate hand-triage (a KB surrogate at ~9125x13293px, far above the 800px elib facsimiles) delineates FOUR layers, only ONE autograph: (1) the 'AD AVGVSTISSIMVM IMPERATOREM RVDOLPHVM SECVNDVM... TYCHONIS BRAHE PRAEFATIO' (front-matter ff. ~img 0010-0018, a multi-page Latin prose address to Emperor Rudolf II) is Tycho's autograph rapid humanist-italic prose — single-storey a, uncial looped d, long-s + round final-s, dense macron suspensions, the looped -que abbreviation, steep ~18-22 deg rightward slant, flourished terminals. It is FIRST-PERSON authorial ('a nobis... exponuntur et demonstrantur', 'in normam ipsi coelo eas exaequavimus', 'Constitui itaque') and carries author-style carets/insertions (img 0011), not the clean ductus of a transcription. Direct comparison against the secure pillar GKS 316 'Ad Daniam Elegia' (autograph, Wandsbek Oct 1597, same months) matches across the diagnostic set. (2) The star-catalogue TABLES (constellation by constellation, img ~0020-0051) and the precession-canon + RA/declination tables (img ~0052-0058+) are a deliberately rounder, slower calligraphic book-hand — a scribe/famulus fair copy, NOT Tycho's running hand. (3) The gilt dedication to Christian IV (img 0007) and the illuminated title (img 0008) are display calligraphy/illumination ('TYCHO BRAHE' on the dedication is built-up gold capitals, NOT an autograph signature). (4) The arched portrait with 16 noble quarterings (img 0009) is a hand-coloured engraving. NB the cursive canon-usage rubrics in the lower-left of the precession tables (img 0019/0052/0055) are in the same cursive as the preface and are a probable autograph annotation of the scribal tables. INVERSION of the Mechanica presentation-copy pattern: there the calligraphic body carries only an autograph signature; here the display is calligraphic but the substantive PREFACE is autograph. A register-symmetric, feature-by-feature comparison of the preface prose against the secure GKS 316 autograph prose (the f.131v departure narrative, 'De occasione interruptarum observationum & discessus mej') returns the strongest band: it supports the same hand, on 25 concordances — 21 of them confirmed on a second audit pass — against 3 discordances, all three on LABILE instrument- and session-dependent traits (pen-pressure contrast, nib width, baseline-drift direction). The two most distinctive concordances carry the case: the leftward-looping uncial d, and the curved, high-placed, concave-up suspension marks; with them run an aligned semi-cursive ductus, habitual pen-lifts before tall d and long-ſ, and an overlapping abbreviation repertoire (nasal macrons, -que, -um, -runt). Caveat (ENFSI BPM-FHX-01): a comparison at these sample lengths is SUPPORTING evidence, not a forensic identification, and no shared capitals were testable. The A grade rests on the CONVERGENCE: (i) Tycho is the author of the preface (first-person address to the Emperor in his own presentation copy), (ii) author-style drafting carets, (iii) full-diagnostic-set paleographic match to the secure pillar, and (iv) the corroborating register-symmetric comparison — not on that comparison alone.

specimens.basis: Body in the SAME cursive register as the signature (no calligrapher break) — a candidate sixth fully-autograph prose pillar. A second comparison, against the secure 14 June 1599 farewell leaf, supports the same hand, where an earlier comparison against the 8 May leaf had been inconclusive. The farewell leaf's pronounced paraph and signature block expose two highly distinctive concordances the 8 May leaf could not test — the two-part signature paraph (horizontal coil with long vertical descender) and the formal-body/enlarged-signature height dichotomy — together with the cursive looped capital A and the long-s/round-s distribution; of the eighteen proposed concordances, sixteen survived audit, and neither of the two proposed discordances did. One DIAGNOSTIC doubt survives: a looped-uncial against straight-ascender d-form, grounded on a single instance in a more formal motto register and plausibly within-writer register variation. Tycho's autograph appears as (a) corrections, marginal computations, headings, date markers — visible by ink/ductus shift — AND (b), newly confirmed from the GKS 316 facsimile, as SUSTAINED autograph PROSE: the 'DE OCCASIONE INTERRUPTArum Observationum & discessus mei' first-person narrative of the April 1597 departure from Hven (f.131v, image TYCH0009) is a whole-leaf autograph in Tycho's rapid humanist-italic prose hand — not merely an intervention. The KB GKS series (1825/1826 'mostly', 311/312 'partly', 316 'partly') is the located corpus. Never assume a tabular Diarium folio is autograph; the autograph is the prose + the interventions.

other_hands.name: Erik Lange (1553-1613), alchemist, Tycho's brother-in-law (m. Sophie Brahe)
other_hands.why: Independent humanist cursive of broadly the same school; co-located in the same album (Sebald Plan, Pillar 2) and circulated through the Brahe-Lange orbit (Sophie Brahe's Eriksholm library).
shared_features: late-16th-c. Northern humanist italic cursive school

discriminating_features.confounder_form: discriminable in detail per Šíma–Valeška (Sebald Plan recto is the Lange reference)

other_hands.name: Peder Jacobsen Flemløse (c.1554-1598)
other_hands.why: First lead assistant (1577-88); observation-log entries; later Bishop of Bergen.

other_hands.name: Gellius Sascerides (1562-1612)
other_hands.why: Hven assistant 1585-92; carried De mundi to Kassel and Tübingen in 1588 (so his hand may appear on De mundi-orbit documents).

other_hands.name: Christen Sørensen Longomontanus (1562-1647)
other_hands.why: The most prolific Tycho-circle copyist (1589-97, returned 1600-01); engrossed most letters and observations. The default author of 'Hven-period Latin' that gets loosely called Tycho's.

discriminating_features.subject_form: Tycho interventions visible as ink + ductus shift (headings, marginal computations, date markers)
discriminating_features.confounder_form: the continuous engrossed body text of letters/observations

other_hands.name: Elias Olsen Morsing (d. 1590)
other_hands.why: Friis (1876) determined by HANDWRITING ANALYSIS that Morsing kept the meteorological diary on Hven for most of 13 Apr 1583 - 5 Apr 1589 — so the 'Tycho's weather diary' is largely Morsing's hand.

other_hands.name: Otto Brahe (Otte Axelsen Brahe, 1579-1611), Tycho's nephew
other_hands.why: Same family/school; album entry co-located in VI F 44 alongside Tycho's.

discriminating_features.feature: (to be characterised against VI F 44 entry)
discriminating_features.confounder_form: Otto's VI F 44 entry — not yet feature-extracted

other_hands.name: Paul Wittich (c.1546-1586), Wrocław mathematical astronomer
other_hands.why: Visited Hven briefly in 1580; his heavily-annotated De revolutionibus (Prague NK 14 B 16) was for over a century described as Tycho's annotated copy. The canonical Tycho misattribution.

discriminating_features.confounder_form: Wittich's characteristic style, independently attested in the BL Sloane + Vatican De revolutionibus copies

discriminating_features.subject_form: Tycho's working notes name Hven / Copenhagen / Uraniborg as base meridian
discriminating_features.confounder_form: Wittich's Vatican 1 (Ottoboniana 1902) flyleaf longitude list names 'Vratislavia' (Wrocław, his home town) but NEITHER Hven NOR Copenhagen (Gingerich) — concrete evidence the notes are Wittich's, not Tycho's. Canonical four-copy confounder set: Liège ResMS 69C, Vatican Ottoboniana 1902, Prague/Klementinum 14 B 16 (=Tres M11), Wrocław 9 (BU 437777); + derivative St Petersburg 1 (Tycho-associated marginalia NOT in Tycho's hand).

misattributions: De revolutionibus marginalia (Prague NK 14 B 16, Basel 1566): reattributed from Tycho to Paul Wittich by Gingerich & Westman 1981 (JHA 12:53–54; full case in the Annotated Census 2002), independently corroborated by Edward Rosen, 'Don't Give Tychon What Isn't Brahe's', Kwartalnik HNiT 26/3-4 (1981) 549–564, and by Šíma–Valeška 2002. THE canonical debunked Tycho-hand claim — in the Debunked Claims Register.

other_hands.name: Professional calligrapher(s) of the presentation copies (≥2 distinct hands)
other_hands.why: Tycho used professional calligraphers to PAINT the bodies of presentation dedications (Mechanica Pillars 3-5; the Tabulae Sinuum; the two Prague trig pamphlets). The body is calligraphic; only the signature is autograph — but the whole leaf gets called 'Tycho's hand'.
shared_features: formal display register superficially resembling Tycho's display-cursive signature

discriminating_features.subject_form: natural cursive rhythm with personal variation
discriminating_features.confounder_form: geometric regularity beyond any cursive hand's natural rhythm
strong display-capital vs minuscule contrast; 'painted' character; pen-lifts every 2-3 letters

misattributions: Triangulorum planorum praxis arithmetica (NK 14 C 20, 1591): Studnička 1901 published as Tycho holograph; Šíma–Valeška: 'undoubtedly the work of a professional calligrapher'. Mathematics is Tycho's; the scribe is not.
Brevissimum planimetriae compendium (NK XII A 28): Studnička 1903 published as Tycho; Šíma–Valeška: a professional writer, and a DIFFERENT one from NK 14 C 20.

other_hands.name: Frans Gansneb Tengnagel von Camp (1573-1636), pupil, son-in-law, posthumous editor
other_hands.why: Took custody of Tycho's instruments and observations after 1601 and edited portions of the Progymnasmata (Prague 1602); many subsequent documents ABOUT Tycho are in Tengnagel's hand and risk being read as Tycho's.

discriminating_features.confounder_form: post-1601 editorial hand on Progymnasmata material

other_hands.name: Tyge Brahe (the son, 1581-1627)
other_hands.why: Tyge sometimes signed AS IF his father, leaving only a 'T(ychonis) F(ilius)' afterthought to distinguish them. A bare 'Tÿcho Brahe' signature could be father or son; he outlived his father by 26 years.

discriminating_features.confounder_form: less practised, slight youthful tentativeness in 1598 (aged 17)

discriminating_features.feature: capital T size + flourish in signature
discriminating_features.subject_form: emphatically display-cursive, large looped ascender + elongated bar
absent — the father signs 'Tÿcho Brahe' / 'manu propria'
discriminating_features.confounder_form: the son appends 'T.F.' after the name
any 'Tÿcho Brahe' signature dated AFTER Oct 1601 is the son

misattributions: Detmold Mechanica dedication (legacy 'Pillar 5b'): signed 'Tÿcho Brahe T.F.', correlates with Tyge's hand (VI F 44 verso), NOT the astronomer — Šíma–Valeška 'Nihil obstat'. A document signed as if by the father, actually by the son.

sources.name: Alvin — platform for digitised cultural heritage (Swedish university libraries)
sources.contributes: Hosts the catalogue record (and image) of the 10 Nov 1598 Dresden 'PLATO' album leaf — Uppsala UB, Waller Ms dk-00231, record 16945 — one of the seven-leaf Wittenberg series. The route to a citable digital surrogate of that specimen.

sources.name: Harald Mortensen, ‘Tycho Brahe-Autografer i Stambøger’, Cassiopeia XIV (1953), pp.94–100
Early Modern Letters Online (EMLO) — Correspondence of Tycho Brahe
sources.contributes: The systematic source for the LETTER corpus' witness/repository metadata — distinguishes surviving autograph ORIGINALS (TBOO 'A' siglum) from drafts/copies ('B') and records holding repositories. This is what's needed to harvest correspondence-register specimens at scale beyond the 3 now in store; the local tekstnet.dk jsonl carries text but NOT the A/B siglum, so the harvest is gated on EMLO's per-letter witness field.

sources.name: Jon Jacobsen Venusinus — 13 facsimiled autographs 1579–1606 (Fund og Forskning 60, 2022, plates)
Owen Gingerich, An Annotated Census of Copernicus' De revolutionibus (Brill, 2002)
Public HTR models for early-modern humanist-italic Latin cursive (Transkribus / eScriptorium survey)
sources.contributes: Surveys the publicly available HTR models that could bootstrap transcription of Tycho's prose hand and the familia scribal hands. As of this build NO Tycho-specific per-hand model exists; generic early-modern Latin / humanist-cursive models would need fine-tuning. Registered to mark the gap honestly: the v1 Graphonomicon ships a grounding pack (atlas + feature model), NOT a trained per-hand model (§7.6 opt-in deferred).

sources.name: Det Kgl. Bibliotek (Royal Danish Library) — soeg.kb.dk catalogue + digital collections
sources.contributes: Holds and catalogues the largest cluster of Tycho autograph and partly-autograph manuscripts: the Hven observation logs (GKS 311, 312, 1825, 1826), the autograph horoscopes (GKS 1822 Prince Ulrik, GKS 1823 Duke Hans), the autograph receipt (NKS 4898), and the 1586 Diarium astrologicum autograph-dedication copy (LN 1170). Each has a stable permalink.

sources.name: Manuscriptorium — European digital library of manuscripts (Czech National Library aggregator)
sources.contributes: Aggregates digitised manuscripts from the Czech National Library, Strahov, and the Národní muzeum — i.e. the institutional homes of Pillars 1-4 (VI F 44, DG IV 25, AG XI 56, III-a-18/1693), the autograph status disputed Tabulae Sinuum (VI E 9), the Bruno Acrotismus (15 K 22), and the two debunked trig pamphlets (NK 14 C 20, NK XII A 28). The single best route to IIIF surrogates of the Prague pillar corpus.

sources.name: Repertorium Alborum Amicorum (RAA) — Stammbuch index, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg
sources.contributes: The largest international album-amicorum index, catalogued down to the individual ENTRY. The instrument for locating the unidentified host albums of the FIVE detached Wittenberg leaves (25 Oct 1598; 16 Apr, 8 May, 29 May, 14 Jun 1599) — searching for Tycho-entry records or for the Jessenský/Peucer-household album owners could re-unite leaves with their original Stammbücher.

sources.name: Edward Rosen, 'Don't Give Tychon What Isn't Brahe's' (Kwartalnik Historii Nauki i Techniki 26/3-4, 1981, 549–564)
sources.contributes: Rosen's corroboration of the Gingerich–Westman reattribution of the De revolutionibus marginalia from Tycho to Paul Wittich. Supplies the Jakob Monau attestation (23 Oct 1600) authenticating the Wittich comet leaves in KB GKS 1826, paleographic plates of both hands (Ryc.1 Tycho / Ryc.2a–e Wittich, same codex/leaf; Ryc.4 Vatican Ottob. lat. 1902; Ryc.5a–g Prague Cimelia), the Wittich library-dispersal narrative (sister in Wrocław → Monau → Tycho), and the edition correction (Prague 14 B 16 = Basel 1566; Nuremberg 1543 = Vatican Ottob. lat. 1902). Also withdraws the Newskaja claim that the Leningrad/Edinburgh De rev. carries Tycho's hand (it is Reinhold's).

sources.name: tekstnet.dk — Det Danske Sprog- og Litteraturselskab (DSL) Tycho Brahe text corpus
sources.contributes: Zeeberg / Gredal Jensen digital edition of the Dreyer Opera Omnia text (509 letters + 56 works), with cross-referenced 1598 foliation. Supplies the diplomatic/normalised TEXT against which the manu-propria letter subscriptions (Scultetus, Savile, Rothmann) and dated formulae can be read — the apparatus layer for the correspondence register. NOT a hand resource (no images), but the authoritative transcription backbone.
